title: YAG Peripheral Iridotomy & The Ando PI
summary: A comprehensive guide to laser photodisruption of the iris. This poster covers clinical indications, precise surgical techniques for both superior and inferior (Ando) iridotomies, and evidence-based management of pupillary block glaucoma.

sections.title: Definition & Mechanism
sections.content: Laser Peripheral Iridotomy (LPI) uses a Neodymium:Yttrium-Aluminum-Garnet (Nd:YAG) laser (1064 nm) to create a full-thickness opening in the peripheral iris. This equalizes the pressure gradient between the posterior and anterior chambers, eliminating pupillary block and allowing the iris to fall away from the trabecular meshwork.

branches: Prophylaxis in fellow eye of AACC

sections.title: The 'Ando' Iridotomy (Inferior PI)
content: Definition: A specific LPI performed at the 6 o'clock position (inferiorly).
Indication: Aphakic or pseudophakic eyes filled with Silicone Oil.
Pathophysiology: Because silicone oil is lighter than aqueous (buoyant), it floats upward and can block the pupil and any superior iridotomies.
Mechanism: An inferior opening (Ando) allows aqueous to flow into the anterior chamber from below, preventing pupillary block by the buoyant oil.
Critical Pearl: Always perform before or during silicone oil injection in aphakic eyes.

sections.title: Pre-Procedure Workup
content: 1. Gonioscopy: Confirm presence of appositional/synechial closure.
2. Van Herick: Slit-lamp estimation of peripheral AC depth.
3. IOP Measurement: Baseline pressure is critical.
4. Medical Prep: 1 drop Pilocarpine 2% (stretch iris) and 1 drop Apraclonidine 1% or Brimonidine (prevent spike).

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Superior PI
content: 1. Anesthesia: Topical Proparacaine/Tetracaine.
2. Contact Lens: Use Abraham or Wise Iridotomy lens with coupling gel (magnifies and concentrates energy).
3. Site Selection: 11 or 1 o'clock (avoid 12 o'clock to prevent air bubble entrapment). Target iris crypt or thinnest area.
4. Firing: Aim for peripheral 1/3 of iris. Apply laser bursts until a 'plume' of pigment and gush of aqueous is seen.
5. Confirmation: Transillumination defect and visualization of lens capsule/zonules through the hole (minimum 0.5mm size).

sections.title: Contraindications & Barriers
content: Corneal Edema (poor visualization/scattering)
Flat Anterior Chamber (risk of corneal endothelial damage)
Neovascularization of the Iris (High risk of massive hyphema)
Severe Intraocular Inflammation (Fibrinous closure risk)
Patient Inability to Cooperate/Stay still

rows: Used for Plateau Iris Syndrome (iris thinning).
Superior for PACG with cataract (EAGLE Study).
Reserved for failed LPI or during other surgery.

sections.title: Post-Operative Regimen
content: Check IOP 30-60 minutes post-procedure.
Topical Steroids (Prednisolone Acetate 1%) QID for 4-7 days.
Continue previous glaucoma drops unless instructed otherwise.
Repeat Gonioscopy in 1-2 weeks to assess angle opening.

content.explanation: Pigment release confirms penetration; Look for the lens capsule; Use a lens for focus; Monitor IOP post-op; Edge of iris (peripheral) is the target.

rows: Prophylactic LPI in PACS patients significantly reduces risk of PAC conversion but has low overall incidence of PAC without treatment.
Clear lens extraction showed better IOP control and quality of life than LPI for PACG and high-IOP PAC.
Established the necessity of the 6 o'clock PI to prevent silicone oil-induced glaucoma in aphakic eyes.

sections.title: Red Flags: Emergency Signs
content: Pressure > 40 mmHg post-op (requires immediate therapy)
Full-thickness Hyphema
Fibrinoid reaction in the anterior chamber
Lens capsule strike (Laser-induced cataract)
Corneal 'pit' or burn

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Success
content: Always treat the fellow eye of a patient with Acute Angle Closure; risk of attack is 50-75% over 5 years.
If the iris is thick/brown, consider 'pre-treating' with Argon laser to thin it before using YAG.
Dysphotopsias (Ting's phenomenon) occur most when the LPI is partially covered by the lid; fully covered or fully exposed is preferred.
The 'plume' of pigment is the most reliable sign of success.
